reason: The key-points card on adv_psychopharm.md lists lithium renal/thyroid/PTH but not lithium levels, and lists clozapine ANC and bowel regimen but no myocarditis surveillance. The page prose says 'vigilance for myocarditis (especially early)' but gives no concrete order, and the card is what gets built into orders. Baseline and early serial troponin/CRP is widely recommended (the Ronaldson protocol; US academic and SMI Adviser guidance), though the US PI does not mandate a schedule. The correction is accurate and fits in place.
evidence: recall (Ronaldson KJ et al., Aust N Z J Psychiatry 2011 monitoring protocol; clozapine US PI myocarditis warning); page prose checked in R01.md
correction: Build monitoring at order entry: lithium levels + renal/thyroid/PTH, clozapine ANC + baseline and early troponin/CRP (myocarditis) + bowel regimen, antipsychotic metabolic panel, QTc when stacking.

reason: The current label (FDA 2025, s016) confirms both indications and the Limitation of Use: effectiveness in preventing suicide or reducing suicidal ideation or behavior has not been demonstrated. The page sentence gives no such caveat, unlike the ECT page and the MDD resident COTW, so it reads as anti-suicidal efficacy. I adjusted the correction to state the label accurately: the MDSI indication applies 'in conjunction with an oral antidepressant'. I also kept 'in TRD' for ketamine.
evidence: SPRAVATO US PI, FDA label 2025 (accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/211243s016lbl.pdf), Indications and Limitations of Use
correction: esketamine (intranasal, REMS-restricted; labeled for TRD and, with an oral antidepressant, for depressive symptoms in MDD with acute suicidal ideation or behavior — though it has not been shown to reduce suicidality itself) and off-label IV ketamine offer rapid antidepressant effect in TRD.

reason: Confirmed on the page: the agitation page's 'Medication principles' paragraph gives an unqualified 'avoid benzodiazepines in delirium and in older adults'. The same page lists withdrawal and catatonia as drivers to exclude, and benzodiazepines are the treatment for both, whatever the patient's age. I extended the exception to cover catatonia, which the page itself names as an agitation mimic.
evidence: recall (ASAM Alcohol Withdrawal Management Guideline 2020; NICE CG103 delirium; BAP catatonia consensus 2023, benzodiazepines first-line); agitation.md context in M05.md
correction: Avoid benzodiazepines in delirium and in older adults, where they tend to worsen confusion — except in alcohol or sedative withdrawal and in catatonia, where they are the treatment.
problem: The blanket 'avoid benzodiazepines in delirium and older adults' has no exception for alcohol/sedative withdrawal delirium or catatonia. The page lists both as drivers to exclude, and benzodiazepines are first-line for both.

reason: The full guideline text (PMC11105801) says CM 'should be a primary component of the treatment plan in conjunction with other psychosocial treatments' (strong). It gives CBT a strong recommendation, CRA and the Matrix Model conditional ones, and bupropion + naltrexone for ATS use disorder a conditional one. 'CM only efficacious intervention' is therefore wrong, and it contradicts canon #180 (ADAPT-2). The correction is accurate.
evidence: ASAM/AAAP Stimulant Use Disorder guideline, J Addict Med 2024;18(1S Suppl 1):1-56, PMID 38669101, doi:10.1097/ADM.0000000000001299 (abstract via PubMed; recommendations 5, 6, 12 via PMC full text)
correction: CM is the standard of care and has the strongest evidence; CBT and community reinforcement approach also recommended, and off-label pharmacotherapy (e.g., bupropion + naltrexone for methamphetamine use disorder) may be considered

reason: The prose 'avoid antipsychotics until catatonia is excluded' has no end point once catatonia is confirmed. The next sentence tells learners to treat the underlying psychosis, and the overlay safety line gives a different end point ('until malignant catatonia/NMS is addressed'). The BAP 2023 consensus allows cautious antipsychotic use once catatonia is treated, with benzodiazepine cover and a lower-D2-affinity agent. I reworded the correction for MS3 level and replaced 'reintroduce', because the patient may never have been on one. The matching pearl ('hold them until catatonia is excluded') needs the same fix.
evidence: recall (Rogers JP et al., BAP consensus guidelines on catatonia, J Psychopharmacol 2023)
correction: **avoid antipsychotics until catatonia is excluded or has responded to treatment** — they can precipitate or worsen NMS and malignant catatonia; if the underlying psychosis then needs one, the team introduces it cautiously, with benzodiazepine cover.
problem: 'Until catatonia is excluded' never ends when catatonia is confirmed, so it implies a permanent ban that conflicts with treating the underlying psychosis and with the overlay's safety line. The same wording recurs in the page's pearl.

The smallest safe change keeps it and adds the label thresholds in label language ('not recommended').
evidence: Lithium carbonate US PI §2.5/§8.6 (via drugs.com/pro/lithium-carbonate.html); Invega Sustenna US PI renal impairment (via drugs.com/pro/invega-sustenna.html)
correction: - **Renal impairment:** dose-reduce **lithium, gabapentin/pregabalin, risperidone/paliperidone, amisulpride** — lithium is not recommended at CrCl <30 and paliperidone palmitate LAI at CrCl <50; paliperidone is heavily renally cleared.
problem: 'Dose-reduce' omits the label thresholds where lithium (CrCl <30) and paliperidone palmitate LAI (CrCl <50) are not recommended at all.

US labels for sertraline, citalopram, escitalopram, paroxetine and fluvoxamine contraindicate starting an MAOI within 14 days, and fluoxetine within 5 weeks. The page ships to US learners, and the correction states both positions accurately.
evidence: recall (US PIs for SSRIs: Contraindications, MAOI within 14 days / 5 weeks for fluoxetine); reviewer's WebFetch of NHS SPS switching guidance
correction: (at least 14 days from most SSRIs per US labeling — UK guidance allows 7–14; at least 5 weeks from fluoxetine)

reason: The finding's premise is that weight gain is one of lithium's most common adverse effects, making it inappropriate to group with low-metabolic-risk agents. The reviewer's own cited meta-analysis says the opposite: lithium weight gain was non-significant (+0.46 kg), no different from placebo, and significantly less than with active comparators. Grouping lithium with the partial agonists as preferable to quetiapine/mirtazapine for a weight-concerned patient is therefore defensible. The page already builds TSH into the pre-lithium workup and notes lithium's monitoring burden. Applying the correction would teach an overstated claim.
evidence: Gomes-da-Costa S et al., Neurosci Biobehav Rev 2021;134:104266, PMID 34265322, doi:10.1016/j.neubiorev.2021.07.011 (PubMed abstract)

reason: This is an omission, not an error. No LAI is mentioned anywhere on the FEP resident page, and APA 2020 statement 10 (2B) supports offering an LAI when the patient prefers it or adherence is poor or uncertain. PRELAPSE (early-phase, <5 y antipsychotic exposure) delayed time to first hospitalization (HR 0.56; 22% vs 36% hospitalized). The quoted sentence is correct as written, so I downgraded to Minor. I tightened the PRELAPSE wording to its actual primary outcome.
evidence: Kane JM et al., JAMA Psychiatry 2020;77(12):1217-1224, PMID 32667636, doi:10.1001/jamapsychiatry.2020.2076; APA Practice Guideline for Schizophrenia 2020 statement 10 (recall)
correction: any taper should be slow, collaborative, and paired with early-warning-sign monitoring and rapid re-engagement plans [3]. Offer a long-acting injectable as a choice, not a punishment — the APA guideline supports it when the patient prefers it or adherence is uncertain, and in early-phase schizophrenia a long-acting injectable delayed first hospitalization (PRELAPSE, 2020).
problem: The relapse-prevention discussion for a first-episode patient with poor insight never mentions offering an LAI, an option supported by the APA guideline and by early-phase trial evidence.

reason: The overlay key point says 'Hold' without qualification, while the body says 'hold/adjust'. Antiepileptics given for epilepsy are continued through ECT (APA Task Force), and in catatonia lorazepam is minimised or timed (flumazenil if needed) rather than stopped. The correction reads grammatically with the retained clause ', and plan continuation treatment…'.
evidence: recall (APA Task Force on ECT, The Practice of ECT 2nd ed. 2001, concurrent medications; Fink & Taylor catatonia literature)
correction: Minimise or time benzodiazepines and mood-stabilising anticonvulsants pre-ECT (they blunt the seizure) — continue antiepileptics prescribed for epilepsy, and don't abruptly stop lorazepam in catatonia
